architecture:
preview = immutable Recon Template + authored Site state + lightweight theme/asset overlays, served by ONE `next start` on a PATCHED COPY of the template app behind ONE stable-URL reverse proxy.
(1) MATERIALIZE (once per template): src/authoring-preview/materialize.ts copies <templateRun>/app into data/<host>/authoring-previews/<previewId>/app, applies two guarded, anchored patches (src/authoring-preview/patch.ts) and runs `next build` ONE time. The reuse key is patchVersion + templateId + the sha256 of the two PRISTINE generated runtime files, so a recompiled template or a changed patch forces a rebuild instead of silently serving a stale app. The immutable template run is a read-only input and is byte-checked untouched (28.P3.37).
(2) CONTENT (hot): the generated runtime memoizes the content contract for the process lifetime and caches each page tree AFTER applySlotContent mutated it — writing WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE has zero effect on a running server. patchSlotContentForAuthoring adds an authoring EPOCH read from its OWN env var WR_AUTHORING_EPOCH_FILE (a tiny file whose entire CONTENT is a monotonic token, written AFTER the overlay file, so a fresh epoch can never point at stale bytes and there is no (mtime,size) collision hole); a changed epoch sets contractPromise=null. patchLoadPageForAuthoring caches the RAW page JSON once per process and keys the APPLIED tree on pageFile|epoch, evicting the page's other epochs. The fresh JSON.parse per epoch is required, not an optimisation: applySlotContent mutates in place and its own expectedValue guard would refuse a second application. Both patches are dead unless WR_AUTHORING_HOT=1. Nothing is patched on the client.
(3) THEME (hot): authored.theme tokens go through generateThemeOverlay — the SAME pure function the theme StageRunner calls — into <preview>/overlay/theme-overlay.css, which the proxy appends to /wr/generated-styles.css after re-reading it whenever its (mtime,size) moves. The served HTML is byte-identical by construction, so a theme edit cannot affect hydration and needs no navigation.
(4) IMAGES (hot): the proxy serves /media/<name> from <preview>/overlay/media first and from the FROZEN materialization second, both by a per-request disk read — the seam src/assets/serve.ts:85 already had. The two changes that make it usable: `cache-control: no-store` in authoring mode (the shipped proxy sends `immutable`, which is why a replaced image was measurably invisible in a browser) and content-type sniffed from the override's bytes (the media name carries the ORIGINAL extension). No media set is copied: one authored replacement is one file write.
(5) EDITOR BRIDGE: an editor-only <script> spliced before </head> of HTML responses only — never into an RSC flight payload — following the shipped src/seo/serve.ts head-splice precedent. It exists only in the proxy process and the bytes it streams; no file inside the app is written.
(6) FALLBACK: `hot: false` restarts the `next start` worker behind the SAME stable proxy URL, which is the parity-qa behaviour kept as the correctness reference.
whyNotTheAlternatives:
WORKER RESTART PER EDIT (candidate A): correct, and already what src/recon-template/parity-qa.ts does, but ~320 ms of every restart is Node/Next process boot that no tuning removes and it discards the warm page cache. Kept as the `hot: false` fallback; measured here as the whole preview start (median 617 ms warm, which INCLUDES boot plus the first page render), i.e. roughly 4x the 144 ms a hot text edit costs end to end.
PROXY VALUE SUBSTITUTION (candidate C): rejected for slot content on evidence, not taste. It addresses a STRING while Slot V2 addresses an OCCURRENCE (pageId/viewport/surface/nodeId/childIndex) and verifies expectedValue before writing. On the linear template 828 of 2441 text slots (34%) share a default value with another slot and 292 default values are a substring of another, so a needle cannot address one occurrence; substitution also discards the expectedValue guard entirely. It stays exactly where it already lives — document-unique strings such as <title> in src/seo/serve.ts.
FULL PRODUCTION BAKE PER EDIT: the baseline being eliminated. Measured on the same site and lineage: runProductionCompile median 3759 ms (n=3) producing a 77.4 MB build directory and a 22.0 MB package, versus 54 ms server-side / 144 ms browser-visible for a text edit.
NEW DOM ATTRIBUTE: no `data-wr-slot` was added. The bridge reports the EXISTING data-wr-node / data-wr-dyn-node plus data-wr-page / data-wr-viewport / route; slot resolution is the editor's job, by inverting slot-bindings.json on (pageId, viewport, nodeId).
productionBakeEvidence: The preview patches a COPY under data/<host>/authoring-previews/; the production compiler copies the immutable template run, so the patched files are unreachable by the bake. Proven, not argued: after a full preview session (materialize + text/url/theme/image edits + browser drive), scripts/smoke-authoring-preview.ts §7 runs the REAL runProductionCompile on the same lineage and walks every file of the produced package — 198 files, 22,042,083 bytes, 0 occurrences of the bridge marker, 0 of the authoring patch marker, 0 of WR_AUTHORING_EPOCH_FILE (28.P3.34-36) — and byte-compares the template run before and after (28.P3.37, 39 files unchanged). Independently reproduced across 3 more compiles in tmp/wr28/preview-scratch/bench2.ts: runs 2026-08-27T12-13-10-354Z / 12-13-14-490Z / 12-13-18-332Z, all 0/0/0. src/production/patch.ts was NOT modified.

editorBridge.originValidation: Outbound: posted to each configured editor origin EXPLICITLY, never "*". Inbound: accepted only when event.origin is in the allowlist AND event.source is window.parent/window.opener AND the payload carries tag "wr-authoring-editor" AND v matches. Measured in a real browser with two same-host DIFFERENT-PORT editor harnesses: the allowlisted one gets ready+pong (28.P3.22/23), the un-allowlisted one receives NOTHING at all and its ping is ignored (28.P3.24).

limitations: EVERY NUMBER IS SINGLE-MACHINE AND SINGLE-SITE FOR THE EDIT METRICS: darwin 25.2.0 / APFS / Node 22 / next 16.3.0 / headless chromium / loopback, on domainchecker.co.kr (19 routes, 1957 slots, 4832 bindings, largest page JSON 292 KB), with other Task-28 phases running concurrently on the same machine. The linear.app canary (8 routes, 2441 text slots, 1.4 MB home page JSON) was exercised for CORRECTNESS only — I did not run the 6-rep benchmark there, so I have no measured edit latency for a large page and I do not claim one.

EVERY EDIT METRIC IS A FULL-DOCUMENT NUMBER. A text or url edit re-parses the whole page JSON on the next request and the browser does a full reload; there is no partial, streaming or diff-based DOM update and no debouncing. An un-debounced keystroke-rate editor would re-parse per keystroke. Debouncing and incremental update are Phase 4's problem and I measured neither.

THE PREVIEW SERVES ONE MEDIA BYTE-STREAM PER MEDIA NAME, NOT A RE-HASHED ASSET. An authored image replacement is written to <preview>/overlay/media/<original-name> and served there, so the preview URL keeps the FROZEN materialization's content hash while carrying different bytes. That is deliberate (it is what makes the edit one file write instead of an assets-stage rerun) but it means the preview's /media path is not content-addressed the way the production artifact's is. The assets StageRunner still does the real, re-hashed materialization at build time.

authored.assets IS CONSUMED BY THE PREVIEW THROUGH A MAPPING I BUILT, NOT THROUGH THE ASSETS STAGE. loadMaterializationLineage composes the materialization manifest (inventoryId → sourceUrl) with the rewrite map (sourceUrl → /media/<sha>.<ext>) to give the media names an assetId is served at. The smoke suite drives replaceMedia by the media names actually present in the rendered DOM rather than by assetId, so the assetId→mediaName mapping itself is exercised by construction (loadMaterializationLineage runs and its rewrite map is what the proxy uses) but is NOT independently asserted by a check. The site-level ids `og-image` / `organization-logo` have no inventory entry and therefore no preview media name at all.

authored.assets[*].alt STILL HAS NO CONSUMER, here as everywhere. The preview replaces BYTES; it does not write markup. An alt edit changes nothing in the preview, exactly as it changes nothing in the bake.

authored.brand IS NOT SURFACED IN THE PREVIEW AT ALL. Nothing in this module reads it. A brand REPLACE/REMOVE/PRESERVE decision is a bake-time IR rewrite owned by the parallel Phase-2 brand builder, so an operator cannot see the effect of a brand decision in this preview.

SEO IS NOT IN THE PREVIEW. The proxy does not rewrite <title>, does not splice the SEO head block and does not serve /robots.txt — src/seo/serve.ts still owns that and was deliberately not chained in. A preview therefore shows the template's own titles, not the production plan's.

PAINT-TWIN AND SVG-TEXT BINDINGS WERE NOT DRIVEN THROUGH THE HOT CYCLE. The linear canary closes the dynamic-template/portal gap the Phase-2 prototyper named (28.P3.38/40, in a real browser), but linear carries only 4 paint-twin bindings and the domainchecker fixture has 0 paint-twin and 0 svg-text bindings, so neither surface is covered by any check here. They go through the same applySlotContent path, which is an argument, not evidence.

CONCURRENCY AND CAPACITY ARE UNMEASURED. One preview server, one browser, one editor. I did not measure multi-tenant memory, simultaneous editors, or what two editors writing the same overlay file do to each other — the epoch ordering makes a single writer safe, and says nothing about two.

THE HOT SEAM IS PROCESS-LOCAL. slotContentEpoch is polled per loadPage call, so a preview whose page cache is never consulted (a route nobody requests) simply re-parses on first request. There is no push, no watcher and no invalidation across processes; a second `next start` on the same preview dir would each hold their own epoch state, which is correct but untested.

THE PREVIEW APP IS A FULL COPY OF THE TEMPLATE APP (39 MB source + a rebuilt .next, ~82 MB on disk for domainchecker, ~100 MB for linear) per template. Copy measured at 49-70 ms on this APFS volume; on a filesystem without cheap clones it will cost materially more and I did not measure that.

THE PRODUCTION-BAKE BASELINE I MEASURED IS domainchecker's (median 3759 ms). It is a small site; the last recorded linear.app bake in this program was ~36 s including the media copy. I did not re-measure linear's bake, so the 'per-keystroke cost avoided' figure quoted here is the SMALL-site figure, which understates the gap on a large one.

I DID NOT WIRE A CLI OR A RELEASE-PROJECT ENTRYPOINT. startAuthoringPreview takes a template run dir plus authored values; it does not yet load a release project, and nothing in src/release calls it. Connecting authored.slotValues / authored.theme / authored.assets straight out of a ReleaseProject is Phase 4 work.

package.json WAS NOT EDITED, per the program contract. The suite is registered only by the appended line in docs/result/handoffs/28-intel/pending-package-scripts.tsv; until an integrator applies it, `pnpm smoke:authoring-preview` does not exist and the suite must be run as `npx tsx scripts/smoke-authoring-preview.ts`.

THE §8 LINEAR CANARY IS SKIPPABLE BY DESIGN (it prints SKIP and drops 4 checks if the linear template run is deleted), following the smoke-regions §7 precedent. That means the suite's check count is 41 with the canary and 37 without — nothing asserts its own total, the same known repo-wide gap the pre-overnight audit recorded.
